correctness.rationale: For d≥2 the rim-only faces are the proper rim subsets and the hub link consists exactly of independent rim sets of size ≤d. Relative chains for the rim inclusion identify the complementary reduced homology naturally and equivariantly with the shifted homology of the independence skeleton; the rim sphere is in a disjoint higher degree. In a skeleton top homology is free, lower homology already equals that of the full complex, and counting cyclic gaps gives the stated Euler characteristic. At d=r+1 the only nonzero map out of a top skeletal homology group is the quotient onto the full cycle-independence homology Z^β; it splits because that target is free. This yields the permanent and one-step integral intervals, not just their field barcodes. For m≥8, r+2≤floor(m/2), so the terminal top group vanishes. In the early range cellular approximation gives the required connectivity of the skeleton; the attaching inclusion in the higher rim sphere is null, giving the asserted wedges. On the complement graph of the rim cycle the signed edge trace minus the vertex trace plus 1 gives all six cases: reflection-swapped adjacent pairs are excluded (one for an odd rim, two for an even edge-axis reflection, none for an even vertex-axis reflection). Every complement edge has an endpoint-swapping reflection, so invariant oriented edge chains, hence invariant H_1, vanish. The rim sign is trivial exactly for m≡1 mod 4; subdivision and rational coinvariants then give the quotient formula.
